# Proto-Humie
Interestingly, the term "Protogen" originates from a Human-created fictional species that shares the same appearance as what are refered to as simply "Protogens"- those without a distinct species.
One could argue humanity invented the Protogen species at large by extension, but, the term was only coined after other races started undergoing the same proceedure.
In fact, it was the advent of Protogen-Vulpkanins in particular that really popularized the name "Protogen" due to the striking resemblance to the fictional race.
## Racial Features - They receive [color=#ffa500]10% more heat damage[/color]. - On top of that, they receive [color=#1e90ff](10%-30%-40%) slash and piercing damage resistance[/color] depending on their cybernetic choice. (Access your species specific loadout from the Appearance tab) - They have a [color=#1fb0ff]Built in MIDI player[/color] - Due to their mixed mechanical and biological nature, they can [color=#1fb0ff]heal with both chemicals and topicals, and welders and wires[/color], however [color=#ffa500]both methods are only 50% effective[/color]. - They are [color=#ffa500]damaged slightly and immobilised by EMPs[/color]. - They have an in-built [color=#1fb0ff]Trinary Radio Channel accessed with the key :D[/color] - Their blood has a dark red color. - Their fists deal [color=red]5[/color] blunt damage with unarmed attacks. - Their standard body heat is 37 degrees Celcius and they can withstand temperatures between -15 and 50 degrees Celcius.
## Sol Common and Trinary The standard language humans speak, known as Sol Common, is composed of a series of short gutteral grunts. It was designed to be simple and easy to learn, allowing most species to be able to produce the sounds required to speak it. Like all other Protogens, they are also able to speak and understand Trinary, a language similar to binary but able to be spoken by most synthetics.
## Age and Names A human's lifespan is considered the standard across the galaxy, as the majority of species have little to no variation from this baseline. They reach adulthood at 18 years of age and are able to live up to 150. Human names are usually given to them by their parents at birth but it is not uncommon to see a human change their own name later in life.
